newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay's Liberals beat Colorados in city election.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay's Liberals beat Colorados in city election.

text.p: Paraguay's Liberal opposition claimed victory over the ruling Colorado Party in Asuncion's key mayoral election on Monday based on partial results released late on Sunday.
In what is viewed as an important indicator for presidential elections due in 1998, Liberal economist Martin Burt, 39, took 51 percent of the vote according to the preliminary results.
Angel Barchini, candidate for the Colorados who have ruled this central South American country for half a century, was running second with 46 percent.
Burt, whose term would end in 2001, hailed the election as a vindication of the fragile democracy that Paraguay has nurtured since Colorado dictator Gen. Alfredo Stroessner was toppled in 1989.
"We have consolidated democracy and voted to continue the changes begun by the first democratic city government in 1991," said Burt, who like Barchini worked for Stroessner.

That 1991 contest for the mayoralty, the second most powerful job in the country after the presidency, was won by a centrist opposition alliance National Encounter, which decided to support the Liberal candidate for mayor this time round.
If their victory is confirmed, the Liberals will take over control of a city of 550,000 inhabitants, but possibly more important will be the impact on the 1998 presidential contest.

"It's a sort of primary to measure the strength of all the presidential candidates for 1998," said political analyst Carlos Martini. Barchini was a stalking-horse for the hardline Colorado presidential hopeful Luis Maria Argana, a fierce critic of current Colorado President Juan Carlos Wasmosy.

"If Argana's faction, represented in Asuncion by Barchini, had won, it would have put Wasmosy in a very tight spot," said Martini. "For the Liberals, Burt's triumph means the launch of another presidential project for 1998."
